✅ **F-2098-1 — F-2090-2 IS ROOT-CAUSED: THE GUARD DEADLOCKS *INSIDE V8*, ON THE WAY OUT, AND THE CONTENTION HYPOTHESIS THREE FIRES CARRIED IS REFUTED (s2098, 2026-08-21)** — F-2090-2 bounded the symptom and left the honest residue *"what does `--report` actually block on when two batteries overlap"*, prescribing a deliberate two-concurrent-batteries reproduction. **That reproduction would have chased the wrong subject: overlap is not the mechanism, and nothing the factory owns is the blocker.** 🔬 **THE EVIDENCE IS A SAMPLED STACK, NOT AN INFERENCE.** The `agent-a7loworbit` orphan F-2090-2 named and deliberately left alive was still running — by then **9 h 39 m elapsed on `0:00.10` CPU** — so s2098 inspected the specimen instead of theorising. `lsof -p 40407`: **cwd + the node binary + dyld, `/dev/null`, two empty kqueues, and fds 0/1/2 as unix socketpairs whose peer is `->(none)`. NO open repo file. NO lock. NO port.** `sample` then produced an unambiguous two-thread deadlock: **main thread** `process.exit()` → `node::Environment::Exit` → `DisposePlatform` → `WorkerThreadsTaskRunner::Shutdown` → `uv_thread_join` → `__ulock_wait`; **V8 worker** `ConcurrentBaselineCompiler` → `BaselineCompiler::Build` → `CodeBuilder::BuildInternal` → `HeapAllocator::AllocateRawSlowPath` → `CollectionBarrier::AwaitCollectionBackground` → `_pthread_cond_wait`. **The main thread is joining the platform workers; a baseline-compiler worker is parked waiting for a GC only the main thread can service. Each waits for the other, forever.** ⚠️ **SO THE SCAN HAD ALREADY FINISHED — IT SIMPLY FAILED TO DIE.** `main()` is fully synchronous with zero pending handles, which is why every corpse holds nothing and burns no CPU. 🪦 **THIS RETIRES THREE INHERITED CLAIMS AT ONCE.** (1) F-2090-2's *"fits the s1536 shared-fixture shape"* — **refuted**: there is no fixture, no file, no lock to share. (2) The prescribed two-battery reproduction — **unnecessary**; load correlates only because it perturbs JIT/GC timing, not because batteries contend. (3) s2097's *"a process at 0.0% CPU cannot contend for a fixture"* reached the **right verdict by the wrong reason** — 0% CPU is not innocence (a process blocked while *holding* a lock is also 0%); the actual reason is that it holds nothing. 💡 **THE REUSABLE HALF: when a hang has outlived its author, the corpse is a WITNESS, not litter — `lsof` + `sample` answer in two minutes what a reproduction plan could not.** F-2090-2 cleared its own two orphans and preserved this one; **that restraint is what made the diagnosis possible five fires later.** ✅ **CURE (`scripts/claimed-spec-harness-guard.mjs`): the three `process.exit()` calls are now `process.exitCode = …` + `return`.** Behaviour-identical (synchronous `main()`, no handles), it lets V8 drain in-flight jobs instead of force-disposing the platform at peak JIT, and it also removes node's known truncation of pending piped stdout. ⚖️ **STATED HONESTLY — THIS SHIFTS PROBABILITY, IT DOES NOT PROVE IMPOSSIBILITY: s2098 could NOT reproduce the deadlock on demand in 180 bounded attempts** (40× the real guard at concurrency 8; 60× and 80× a synthetic of the same shape, the latter under `--max-old-space-size=24 --max-semi-space-size=1`) — **zero hangs.** The race is rare; the claim is limited to removing the *guaranteed*-in-flight window that a force-exit creates. s2090's `SPAWN_LIMITS` timeout stays as the bound, and is now a bound with a diagnosis attached. 🔒 **GUARDED (`claimed-spec-harness-guard.test.mjs`, 12/12): a source-level assertion that the guard never calls `process.exit(` again — RED PROVEN BY MANUFACTURING THE DEFECT: restoring the force-exit fails exactly ONE test, mine, while the other 11 stay green.** That asymmetry is the whole reason it exists — the three existing `r.status` assertions pass whichever way the exit is written, so nothing already in the file would have noticed someone "tidying" it back. ⓘ **SCOPE DELIBERATELY NOT WIDENED:** `process.exit()` is the house pattern across the guard corpus (`desk-carryforward-guard` 4×, `status-archive-audit` 3×, `attended-owed-audit` 1×, `nul-audit` 1×), and a blanket rewrite is neither evidence-backed nor a fire's call — **only this script has actually hung, three times, and it is the leaf both F-2090-2's orphans and s2097's 120 s timeout named.** If a second guard is ever sampled in this stack, cure the class then. 🧹 **The pid-40407 specimen was LEFT ALIVE AGAIN, consistent with s2090's ruling that another context's orphan is not a fire's to reap — but it is now a *confirmed* corpse rather than an unknown: it is deadlocked by construction and can never make progress, so whoever reaps it is destroying nothing.**

🟡 **F-2087-3 — `status-archive-audit` CANNOT EVER CLEAR AN ATTENDED-AUTHORED LINE-1, SO ITS RED HERE IS UNFIXABLE BY THE FIRE IT ACCUSES (measured s2087, VERIFIED by reading the predicate).** `sessionOf()` (`scripts/status-archive-audit.mjs:53`) recognises exactly two ownership shapes — `s<N> fire` and `s<N> handoff` — so a line-1 written by an ATTENDED session (`ACTIVE 2026-08-20T15:58Z (attended drain) — …`, no s-number anywhere) resolves to `lostSession === null`. The permanence predicate then reads `rec.permanent = rec.lostSession === null || !<archive-bullet regex>` — **the null short-circuits to TRUE before the archive check is ever consulted**, so no bullet, however correct, can mark it restored. 📊 **Measured this fire:** the audit reported 2 permanently-lost line-1s in its 40-commit window; I recovered BOTH verbatim from git and re-archived them (`c43799bc2`). The s2086 one (8,193 chars, `s2086 handoff`) was immediately recognised — **LOST fell 2 → 1**. The attended lock line (263 chars) is byte-present at HEAD (`grep -c` = 1) and still reports LOST. 🚫 **DO NOT CURE THIS BY RELABELLING THE BULLET with an invented `s<N>` prefix.** That would write a FALSEHOOD onto the board — that some numbered fire owned a line the attended session wrote — purely to satisfy a string match. The script's OWN comment block at `:138–:149` forbids exactly this class of remedy, in the same words, for the sibling F-1690-2 case: *"A guard whose remedy is to corrupt a correct file is the guard that is wrong."* ⚠️ **AND THIS WILL GET WORSE, NOT RARER:** F-1546-1 already recorded that the factory's drain load has moved to attended sessions, and attended line-1s carry no s-number by convention — so every attended lock line that a later session archives correctly will red here forever, training readers to excuse this guard the way `cross-engine` got excused (F-1460-1). **RECOMMENDED CURE (fire-authorable, small):** teach `sessionOf()` an attended shape (e.g. `(attended …)` → a stable `attended-<stamp>` key) and match the archive bullet on that same key, keeping the `(line-1 archive` phrase binding so an unarchived line still reds. **NOT DONE HERE:** it edits a sanctioned guard and deserves its own master with a manufactured-red proof in both directions. **GATE: `test:ledger-guards` stays rc=1 on this single attributed line until the cure lands — the red is KNOWN, NAMED and ATTRIBUTED, not unexplained.**

✅ **F-2083-1 CURED s2083 — MAIN WAS RED FOR EVERY FIRE AND THE FIX NEEDED NO SCHEMA CHANGE AT ALL.** `scripts/goal-tracker.test.mjs` was failing on **pristine main** (controlled: reproduced with no merge applied), which reds `test:node-guards` **and** `test:ledger-guards` — the very battery the s1301 law makes every fire run as its last act, so every fire was inheriting a red it did not cause. 🔎 **FOUR violations, not the one that was visible.** An independent sweep of the whole tree (a third implementation of the question, not the guard's) found **2 leaves × 2 defects**: `e2-pressure-arsenal-headless` and `showroom-cap-fix` each carried a **prose `taskFile`** (`"ATTENDED-AGENT (no lane master; dispatched via Agent tool per owner engine directive)"`, violating `:79`) **and a 9-char short `mergeHash`** (`19dd85c0a`, `f8d025747`, violating `:80`'s `/^[0-9a-f]{40}$/`). ⚠️ **The `mergeHash` half was invisible: `:79` asserts first, so it aborted the leaf check before `:80` ever ran — fixing only the reported defect would have re-redded on the next line.** Assertion order hides siblings; sweep the class, never the message. 🎯 **AND THE SCHEMA WAS NEVER THE PROBLEM — `:79` reads `if (leaf.taskFile)`, i.e. the field is ALREADY OPTIONAL.** The owner's engine directive created a real dispatch mode (Agent tool, no lane master) that genuinely has no `.md` file; the prose was simply put in a filename field. The truthful record is to **omit** `taskFile` and keep the wording verbatim in `note` (prefixed `DISPATCH:`) — supersede, never erase. **No guard was loosened, no sentinel invented, no `.md` fabricated that does not exist.** The two short hashes were expanded to their full 40 chars after verifying each resolves to a real commit whose subject matches its leaf title, so the merge evidence was genuine all along — only abbreviated. **VERIFIED:** `goal-tracker.test.mjs` **2/2 green on main** (29.7 s); independent re-sweep reports **0 remaining schema violations**. 🔻 **AND ONE PREDICTION OF MINE WAS REFUTED, RECORDED BECAUSE IT WAS TESTED:** the s2083 review first claimed fixing this would also clear `fixture-teardown` (F-2083-3). F-SR-5 IS A TWO-AXIS MAPPING QUESTION AND IS NOT FIRE-AUTHORABLE.** `reviews/assay-season-roll.md:17` files F-SR-5 as *"(player-visible, one-param fix)"* with the cure already *"proven by the agent's own battery: `?view=byStack&season=1` merges through existing `mergeFieldBooks`"*. Measured at source before authoring anything against it, and the cure does not survive the reading. The reader's `loadSeasonResults(seasonId)` (`src/encyclopedia/reader.ts:538-552`) sets `view` and `epoch` and **never sets `season`** — that half of the finding is TRUE and the page really does read the wrong ledger post-roll. But the value it holds is a **CHRONICLE** id: `SEASONS` (`src/seasons/registry.ts:10-20`) are `founding-season` / `same-game-season`, **strings**, while `parseSeason` (`functions/api/standings.ts:933-938`) accepts only `/^[0-9]{1,4}$/` ∈ `KNOWN_SEASONS = {1,2}` and returns `null` otherwise → `:287` refuses with **400 `bad_season`**. So `url.searchParams.set('season', seasonId)` — the literal one-param fix — **breaks the page instead of fixing it**, and the working version requires deciding that the founding *chronicle window* corresponds to *ledger* season 1. ⚠️ **THAT DECISION IS THE THING THE SOURCE FORBIDS TAKING CASUALLY:** `standings.ts:161-168` says the two axes "are genuinely different and **must never be conflated**", that the chronicle "partitions by WHEN a row was posted; its current window already contains pre-assay rows, **so it cannot express the roll**", and — in the same breath — that season pages were deliberately left alone: *"Untouched here: rows keep their chronicle name and the season pages keep telling the story."* The windows do not align by construction, so no mapping is a mere lookup. ➡️ **THEREFORE F-SR-5 IS ATTENDED/OWNER-GATED, NOT FIRE-AUTHORABLE**, and §2E's hard limit applies verbatim: *needs a design fork → do NOT author*. The cheap-looking fix is the trap. 💡 **THE CLASS, and it is the third time in this one fire that re-verifying an inherited claim overturned it:** a finding's *cure* is a claim exactly as much as its *defect* is, and the two can have opposite truth values — here the defect is real, the cure is wrong, and the word "proven" was carried from a battery that proved something adjacent (that `mergeFieldBooks` merges a season-scoped payload) rather than the fix itself. **A cure inherits its author's confidence, not their evidence — re-derive the lever, never the conclusion.** (Same family as F-1590-1's prove-the-lever rule, arriving from the ledger side rather than the master side.)

I went to do exactly that and the premise did not survive the first probe. ✗ **The spec slice (`specs/agent-play/ap-16-same-game-law.md:35`) classifies five verbs as OWED — `TOGGLE_WEAPON` · `RESEARCH_PICK` · `SECURE_CHOICE` · `DEATH_ACTION` · `CONTEXT_ACTION` — and closes with *"Each verb: same rules, same costs, additive hashes."* **That closing promise is measurably false for all five**, because the systems they would drive do not exist headless.** 🔬 **MEASURED, file by file, not inferred from the audit table:** **(1) `TOGGLE_WEAPON`** — `weaponToggle` is consumed in exactly ONE place in the whole tree, `src/game/Game.ts:2473` (`if (intents.weaponToggle) this.toggleWeapon()`), which is the BROWSER game. There is no headless weapon state to toggle. **(2) `RESEARCH_PICK` / `SECURE_CHOICE` / `DEATH_ACTION`** — `grep` for `research`, `secureChoice`, `deathAction` and `secure_choice` over `src/sim/HeadlessContractSim.ts` returns **zero hits each**, and the sim's 36 imports compose no research, secure-choice or death-action system (the single `esearch` hit anywhere under `src/sim/` is `E9ArsenalSocket.ts`, an unrelated arsenal surface). ⚖️ **WHY THAT MAKES IT NON-AUTHORABLE RATHER THAN MERELY BIGGER:** adding any of these verbs means **porting a system into the sim**, which changes what the sim DOES — hero attack resolution for the weapon, run-end agency for secure/death — and therefore **moves event-log hashes**, contradicting the slice's own additive promise and every "additive, default preserves every existing hash" assertion AP-16-4/5 landed on. I did **not** verify the opportunity cost (it lives in `Game.ts`'s attack path, outside what this probe read), so this is stated as the question it is, not as a finding. **GATE: ATTENDED — re-slice AP-16-6 against its real implementation surface.** The three live options, none of which a fire may pick: **(a)** port the systems and accept an era re-stamp for the hash movement; **(b)** rule the five verbs EXEMPT-with-cited-reason as browser-input artifacts with no headless referent, which is the *"exemption is a debt, not a policy"* path AP-16-4 already established; **(c)** decide the `BLAST_AT`-vs-toggle equivalence question above first, since a ruling that agents already have ability parity may retire `TOGGLE_WEAPON` outright. ⓘ **No goal leaf exists for AP-16-6** (`drain-block-check ap16-6` → UNKNOWN, and a `goals.json` walk for `ap16-6` returns `[]`), so nothing on the board is left stale by not authoring it.

🔵 **F-1648-2 (s1648 2026-08-11, CURED IN THE SAME FIRE — THE FACTORY REPORTED `RESUMED` WHILE ITS IMPLEMENT SIDE WAS DEAD, AND IT STAYED DEAD BECAUSE TWO SEPARATE `pgrep -f` CHECKS EACH MATCHED THE COMMAND THAT WAS RUNNING THEM).** The resume one-liner was `until ! pgrep -f "FIRE PROTOCOL"; do sleep 15; done; nohup bash scripts/lane-runner-v3.sh …`, run as one backgrounded shell. **Both of its guards are self-matching, because the whole command line — including its own search strings — is the argv `pgrep -f` searches:** (a) the wait loop matches its own shell forever, so the restart it guards **can never fire**; (b) `lane-runner-v3.sh`'s otherwise-correct stale-lock self-heal — *"if no OTHER runner process exists, the lock is a corpse"* — counted that same wrapper as another runner, declined to clear the corpse lock left by the killed loop, and logged *"another instance running … Remove if stale."* **Net effect: the ops commit says the runner was restarted, `tasks/.runner.lock` was a month-old corpse, and no runner process existed at all.** ⚠️ **The dangerous part is not the outage, it is that the LEDGER SAID OTHERWISE** — Mistake #4's shape at factory scale: a fire reading the resume commit inherits *"runners restarted"* and never probes. ✅ **CURED s1648**: corpse lock cleared, runner started detached with `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` **scrubbed from its environment** (a runner started from a fire shell would otherwise inherit the fire's config dir and silently pin every LANE playwright run to `workers: 1` via the `isFireShell` key in `playwright.config.ts` — §3.1's mechanism firing in exactly the direction it is written to forbid), and verified up by pidfile+log rather than by the fact that the command returned. 💡 **GENERAL: `pgrep -f <string>` run from a shell whose own command line contains `<string>` always finds itself. Any liveness probe written inline in the command it is probing for is a tautology** — probe from a script file, or match a pattern the probing command cannot contain.

🔵 **F-1648-3 (s1648 2026-08-11, RESTORED IN THE SAME FIRE — A FIRE KILLED MID-CYCLE TAKES ITS PREDECESSOR'S HANDOFF WITH IT, BECAUSE THE ARCHIVE DUTY IS DISCHARGED AT HANDOFF TIME AND A KILLED FIRE NEVER GETS THERE).** s1647's lock commit replaced line-1 without archiving s1646's handoff — the **normal** pattern, which `status-archive-audit` scores as normal precisely because the fire's own handoff commit restores it. Any fire taking over a lock it did not set should `grep -c` for its predecessor's predecessor before assuming the chain is intact** — the cost is one command and the loss is otherwise silent.

🔵 **F-1639-1 (s1639 2026-08-10, FOUND AT THE sea-2 DRAIN — NON-BLOCKING, GATED, CURE OUTSIDE THIS SLICE'S FIREWALL): the grouped standings API keeps ONE cell per group×contract, so a second season's page will UNDER-REPORT and its honest-empty line will become a FALSE statement.** The runner reported this itself as *"the grouped API loses cross-season cells"*; I verified it in code rather than taking it. `functions/api/standings.ts:324` guards cell creation with `if (!group.contracts.has(contractId))`, so the first row wins and the cell carries **only that row's** season; `src/encyclopedia/reader.ts` then filters with `cell.season === season` and drops a row whose cells all fall away. **Vacuous today — exactly one season exists, so every cell carries the same label or none.** The day Season 2 opens: a Mind whose best ride on a contract was in Season 1 has no cell for Season 2 and vanishes from its page, and if that empties the page the county says *"No rides were posted for this season"* — **which would be false.** That is the sharp edge, and it is worse than a missing row because it reads as a fact. Unfixable in SEA-2 by design: the cure is a per-season cell projection in `functions/**`, which SEA-2's master firewalled by name (*"if you find yourself wanting a new field, you are solving it in the wrong place"*). Scope: a SEA-1 follow-up or SEA-4. **GATE: before any season is given a `startsAt` that puts two seasons live at once — i.e. before the Season-2 boundary is minted, which ap16-2b's merge makes possible.**
🔵 **F-1639-2 (s1639 2026-08-10, FOUND AT THE sea-2 DRAIN — NON-BLOCKING, PRE-DATES THE SLICE, RECORDED FOR ACCURACY): a MISSING KV binding presents as an honest-looking empty county; a per-contract THROW does not.** The sea-2 runner reported that the API *"masks per-contract KV failures"*. Half true, and the half that is not matters, so it is written down rather than repeated: at `functions/api/standings.ts:171` an absent binding yields `kv ? await readBoard(...) : []` for every contract and the response is `ok: true` with zero rows — indistinguishable from a genuinely empty county. **But** a `readBoard` throw rejects the enclosing `Promise.all` and surfaces as a 500 *"The county book is unavailable"* through the outer catch, so real per-contract failures are NOT swallowed. Neither behaviour is introduced by SEA-2, and SEA-2's client already separates *unavailable* from *empty* on its own side (its third test exists precisely to hold that line). **No action owed; recorded so the next reader does not inherit the stronger claim.**

🟢 **F-1595-2 (s1595 2026-08-09, HIT AND CURED IN THE MANDATORY POST-HANDOFF BATTERY — THE HOUSE BANNER CONVENTION SILENTLY UN-DECLARES ANY DESK ITEM WHOSE ROW IT BANNERS).** Non-blocking, cured this commit, and filed because the convention is two fires old and WILL recur. ⚙️ **THE COLLISION:** the banner convention minted by F-1594-1 prepends `⛔ **CURED — DO NOT AUTHOR…**` immediately after a row’s leading marker, preserving the original wording behind it (Retention Law). But `scripts/desk-declaration-guard.mjs` requires a desk item’s declaring row to carry that item’s key **as its FIRST key, within the first 90 characters** — so a banner longer than ~85 chars **pushes the row’s own F-ID out of the declaring zone and the item silently becomes undeclared.** ✓ **MEASURED, not reasoned:** bannering `F-1364-1` — a live desk item (the AP-03/04/05 re-greenlight, *“ONE WORD unblocks THREE leaves”*) — took the guard to `undeclared: 1 · FAIL`. ⓘ **s1594 minted the convention and did not hit this, by luck alone: none of its four bannered rows (`F-1565-2`/`F-1515-2`/`F-1551-1`/`F-1549-2`) was a desk item.** The convention has therefore been latent-defective since birth and looked perfectly safe for a full fire. ➡️ **CURED — the fix is a keystroke and should become the convention: restate the row’s own key immediately after the marker, banner second** — `🟡 **F-1364-1** ⛔ **CURED — …**` — which satisfies the guard, keeps the banner prominent, and preserves the original wording verbatim behind both. Same seam-between-two-correct-procedures class as [[F-1595-1]] — and found the same way, by running the thing afterwards instead of reasoning about it.*

🟢 **F-1595-1 (s1595 2026-08-09, MEASURED + CURED THIS FIRE (6 rows) + THE NARROW ARM BUILT AND MEASURED — THE HEADER-SCAN CLASS RE-ARMS ITSELF ONCE PER SHIPPING FIRE — BUT MY OWN "MISTAKE #8 ARMED" SEVERITY CLAIM WAS REFUTED BY PROBE IN THIS SAME FIRE, AND THE REFUTATION IS THE MORE USEFUL HALF).** Non-blocking. Discharges s1594’s (B) and (C). ✓ **(B) THE FOUR UNJUDGED F-1594-1 RESIDUE ROWS ARE JUDGED — 1 BANNERED, 3 CLEAR, each by probe not by prose.** `F-1364-1` **BANNERED** (cure `6d7f888f` confirmed an ancestor of main; `tasks/goals.json` carries the owner’s full conjunction + `DO NOT AUTHOR OR QUEUE` on both `ap-03-protocol` and `ap-04-teach`). `F-1368-1` **CLEAR** (`5570b457e` rebuilt `docs/MAP-CAMPAIGN-LEDGER.md`, `landmarks` column present). `F-1357-1` **CLEAR** (`BACKLOG.md:2948` reads `✅ RETIRED s1357`; its tail explicitly rules the remainder owner-gated, NOT fire-authorable). `F-1347-1` **CLEAR** (`f6af7eae` on main; its own tail states `GATE: none — closed by the patch`). 🔑 **THE DISCRIMINATOR, AND IT IS ONE WORD: `MEASURED` IS A VERB ABOUT THE INVESTIGATION, NOT ABOUT THE DISPOSITION.** The three clear rows lead with `CORRECTED` / `EXECUTED` / `PATCHED`; the one bannered row leads with `MEASURED` alone. s1594 hunted this class with a vocabulary of `CLOSED s<N>`/`ABSORBED` plus the marker and called its own pass-1 under-counting; the actual test is cheaper and sharper — **does the header zone contain ANY past-tense disposition verb?** A header that says only MEASURED has told the reader an investigation happened and nothing about what became of it. ⚠️ **(C) I BUILT s1594’S RECOMMENDED NARROW MERGE-HASH ARM, AND IN ITS RECOMMENDED FORM IT DOES NOT SURVIVE CONTACT WITH THE LEDGER — RECORDED SO NOBODY BUILDS IT TWICE.** `scripts/tmp-s1595-tail-closure-scan.mjs`, run over the live board: **1,353 F-ID rows · 503 carry an open-ish marker with no closure verb in the first 260 chars · 62 name a cure-at-hash in the tail · 61 of those hashes are ancestors of main.** **61 of 503 is a 12% red rate on correctly-written rows**, because a row legitimately stays open while citing the hash of a shipped CHILD or a half-landed cure. That is the exact fate s1594 predicted for the *judgement*-shaped guard (excused into uselessness, the `cross-engine` fate F-1460-1) — **and it applies equally to the arm s1594 recommended instead.** A narrower aim was needed, not a narrower vocabulary. ✅ **RE-AIMED AT THE SUB-CLASS WHERE THE QUESTION IS THREE FACTS AND NO JUDGEMENT — DISPATCH ROWS.** `scripts/tmp-s1595-dispatch-row-scan.mjs`. A dispatch row does not describe a problem, it **advertises a queueable master BY PATH**, so the conjunction is checkable: *header invites dispatch and declares no closure* **AND** *tail says shipped at a hash `git merge-base --is-ancestor` places on main* **AND** *the master file is still on disk and therefore still `cp`-able*. **322 rows cite a `tasks/*.md` path · 19 header-invites · 5 ARMED, and all five masters were still on disk.** ⚠️ **THE DENOMINATOR WAS WRONG ON FIRST PASS AND I VARIED THE PATTERN RATHER THAN TRUSTING IT** (a class-grep reports its hits and never its misses): the first regex required `**slug** \`tasks/x.md\`` and saw **15** rows, while `grep` for a backticked `tasks/*.md` path anywhere saw **322**. With `stepSeconds = FIXED_SIM_STEP_SECONDS = 1/30` (`Game.ts:953`): **live** = 30 ticks/real-second, `presentationAt` **1/30 s per tick**, `timeAlive` `(1/30)×4` = **2/15 per tick**; **manual** = `presentationDelta` `(1/30)/4` = **1/120 s per tick** (`Game.ts:6831`), `timeAlive` `(1/120)×4` = **1/30 per tick** (`Game.ts:6843`). **Both ratios exactly 4.** ➡️ **So at a given tick count the pinned sweep has advanced the simulation's own clock four times less far than the live loop had** — `timeAlive` being what feeds sim-side behaviour (`echoBoss.observe(…, this.timeAlive)`, `decay`, `StandingOrders`). The runner's headline was **exactly right**; only its attribution of the consequence to the idle bob was wrong, and by (2) the bob could not have mattered either way. **The conclusion below is unchanged and now rests on verified evidence.** 💡 **THE LESSON, AND IT REPEATED INSIDE THIS ROW: the runner asserted a mechanism, this row elaborated it confidently, and the first correction over-reached in the opposite direction. Three readings, two wrong, every one of them plausible.** The stable facts came only from opening `Embodiment.ts`, `Balance.ts`, the spec's `distance()` helper, and `Loop.ts`'s constructor and `setTimeScale` callers. ⭐ **The one claim that never wobbled is the one that needed no causal story at all — a Y-axis bob cannot move an x/z metric. Prefer the check that requires no mechanism over the mechanism you find convincing.** It cost nothing only because `/author-task` §0.2 forced the files open before scope was written. ⛔ **THEREFORE THE `0.35324532108975587` MARGIN WAS MEASURED WITH THE DOMINANT ERROR TERM SUPPRESSED AND MUST NOT BE CARRIED INTO A RE-PIN OF THE LIVE-LOOP `m4-06` ASSERTION** (F-1441-3 still binds: re-pin only with a named cause, never to green a red). *"No band at any start phase"* is sound **about the manual-sim regime** and is **not** evidence that start phase is irrelevant in the live regime where the breach was actually seen. 🔑 **THE GENERAL SHAPE, which is the reusable half: a harness built to CONTROL a variable can control it by REMOVING the phenomenon.** Pinning the tick was supposed to isolate phase; it instead changed the tick↔`timeAlive` ratio, and a ratio change is a regime change. 🟡 **F-1516-2 (s1516 — A DONE-MOVE'S MTIME IS ITS QUEUE-INSERTION TIME, NOT ITS COMPLETION TIME, SO §2B'S OWN DRAIN TRIGGER IS WRONG IN THE STARVING DIRECTION.** Non-blocking, but it can silently cost a whole fire's drain.) `scripts/fire.md` §2B tells a fire to drain *"done-moves in `tasks/done/` newer than the last handoff"*. 📐 **THE MECHANISM, measured on this fire's own dispatch rather than inferred:** the lane runner `mv`s the queue file into `tasks/done/` **at COMPLETION** — but `mv` **preserves the mtime the file acquired when it was `cp`'d into the queue at DISPATCH**. Timeline, three independent clocks: master written **09:32:08** · done-move mtime **09:34:13** (the `cp`) · run-log last write **09:39:27** (the actual completion). So `ls -lt tasks/done/` sorts by **dispatch** order and every done-move's mtime **understates** completion — here by ~5 minutes, and for `f1515-1` by **27**. ⚠️ **THAT GAP IS EXACTLY WHERE A DRAIN GETS SKIPPED, and it nearly happened this fire:** `f1515-1` was queued **09:07**, completed **~09:34**, and its done-move carries mtime **09:07** — **older than s1515's 09:21 handoff**. A fire obeying §2B's sentence literally would have concluded there was nothing newer than the last handoff and **skipped a finished, gated, mergeable slice**; I found it only because I listed `tasks/runs/` and read a log tail. It merged as `8b853308`. 💡 **The trap is that the rule LOOKS self-checking** — a timestamp compared against a timestamp — which is why it survived; nothing about `ls -lt` announces that one of the two clocks belongs to a different event. ⓘ **I first mis-diagnosed this as "the runner done-moves at dispatch"** (which would have meant a done-move proves only that a run STARTED) and wrote that into my handoff before measuring it; the three-clock comparison above refuted my own correction. **A done-move DOES mean the run finished — its mtime just does not say when.** **REC: trigger §2B on the RUN LOG's mtime (which is written at completion) or on `git log main..lane/*` (content, not clocks), and treat `tasks/done/` mtimes as dispatch order only.** Related: [F-1516-1], [F-1300-4].

🟡 **F-1516-1 (s1516 — A PROBE CAN VALIDATE THE RIGHT MECHANISM THROUGH THE WRONG MODULE SYSTEM, AND THE CONJUNCT IT "PROVED" IS THE ONE NOBODY RE-EXAMINES.** Non-blocking; no corrective queued — recorded as a class, and the cure is already named in the row above.) s1516 priced the F-1510-3 successor with deliberate rigour: it asked the [F-1514-1] question **conjunct by conjunct** — *would performing this scope make the gate sentence TRUE?* — and tabled five answers. **Four were right. The fifth was wrong, and it was the one backed by an EXPERIMENT rather than by reading.** 🔬 **THE MECHANISM:** the decisive probe ran in `/tmp/s1516-pw-probe`, a directory with **no `package.json`**, so Playwright transpiled its TypeScript config to **CommonJS**, where `__dirname` exists — and it duly returned a real sha (`6e21f9831909…`, the fire's own lock commit), which read as conclusive. This repo is **`"type": "module"`**, so the identical config loads as **ESM** and `__dirname` is undefined. **The probe matched its subject on flags and on Playwright version, but not on COMPOSITION**, and the pricing doc plus the authored master both went on to *mandate* `__dirname`. Cost: one lane run (92,161 tokens), recovered in full because the master licensed exactly this negative result and named `__dirname` as a candidate failure. ⚠️ **THE GENERAL SHAPE, which is what makes this worth a row:** a conjunct you verified by *reasoning* stays visibly provisional and gets re-read; a conjunct you verified by *running something* acquires the authority of a measurement and is never revisited. **So the audit question is not "did I test it?" but "did my test share the subject's composition?"** — module system, runtime, config loader, and package boundary are all part of a probe's claim, not its scenery. 💡 Same family as [a control arm must match in composition, not just flags] and [a probe that dies in your stub is evidence about your stub], but a distinct and nastier polarity: **this probe did not die and did not mislead by failing — it PASSED, and the pass is what did the damage.** **REC (process, not code): when a probe is built OUTSIDE the subject tree for isolation, state in the pricing which properties of the subject the probe does NOT reproduce, and treat every one of them as unproved.** Isolation and representativeness trade against each other, and the trade should be written down rather than discovered by a runner. Related: [F-1510-3], [F-1514-1].

GATE: closes when a bare-name query is refused rather than answered, and the verdict line carries the date.** Related: [F-1508-1], [F-1507-2], [F-1506-2].

**GOAL REGISTRATION LAW (owner ask, 2026-07-16): every authored master adds its leaf to `tasks/goals.json` in the same commit; every drain updates that leaf's status and merge hash.** A task is not fully authored or drained until both the backlog and goal tree tell the same truth.

**Stale-check law**: a master written >2 days ago gets a 60-second reality check against current main before queueing (the m4-02 "6→40 refresh" lesson) — refresh it or flag it, never blind-queue. ⚠️ **ITS SUBJECT IS A MASTER, AND THAT IS THE HOLE F-1344-1 FELL THROUGH (s1344): a ladder RUNG that has no master yet is never stale-checked by anyone, because there is no file whose age to measure.** The 079a offer sat 21 days describing shipped work. **Stale-check the RUNG before you author, not just the master before you queue.**

🟢 **F-1421-1 (s1421, MEASURED AND RULED — A RESIDUE COUNT IS ONE-DIRECTIONAL, SO A FOUR-FIRE PRIORITY WAS BUILT ON A NUMBER THAT COULD NOT MEAN WHAT IT WAS READ TO MEAN.)** s1419 shipped the line-level residue instrument and immediately used it to re-price lane-b, reporting *"the entire real residue is ~13 lines across 7 paths"* and concluding this was *"a cheap, well-lit job for the next fire."* s1420 and s1421's own lock inherited that framing. **The 13 is exactly right and the conclusion does not follow.** `residueFor()` answers *are these added lines absent from main's current text?* — it cannot distinguish **absent because main never saw it** from **absent because main saw it and moved past it** (supersession) or **absent because main took the same content by a different commit** (re-landing). All three read identically. On lane-b, **zero** of the 13 turned out to be the first kind: 5 superseded, 8 owner-blocked, and the two commits carrying the superseded lines had been re-landed to main at s1392/s1394 — *a day before the instrument that re-priced them was written.* ⓘ **This is not a defect in `lane-residue.mjs` and no cure is proposed:** the tool measures what it claims to measure, its own docs say so, and F-1419-1 pinned the threshold that keeps it honest in the destructive direction. 🟢 **F-1397-3 (s1397, MEASURED) — `citation-title-guard`'s quote extraction desynchronises on short inline-code spans, so a correct citation can red for reasons in the prose beside it.** Its `QUOTED` regex treats every backtick, straight quote **and apostrophe** as a delimiter and requires 12–160 characters between a pair, so **an unpaired quote character shifts the pairing for everything after it**. Two triggers were measured, both in ordinary prose: an inline-code span shorter than 12 characters (skipped as an opener), and — caught only when this very row first reddened the guard — **a possessive apostrophe, as in "E1's", which is an unpaired delimiter the writer never thinks of as one.** In both cases — the regex then captures the prose *between* code spans instead of the spans themselves. Measured: a verbatim quote of a real source line sat inside the window and was never extracted, because a nearby 9-character span had offset the pairing. Two neighbours worth knowing: the window is ±400 characters, so a citation's verdict can depend on where that window happens to start; and `MIN_PREFIX` is 20, so a 19-character quoted prefix fails. **NOT filed as a defect to fix** — the guard's purpose (recoverability) is served and loosening the regex risks false greens. **Recorded as a cure for the next reader:** put the quote immediately after the citation, in double quotes, with no inline-code spans between them. **GATE: none — informational.**

The tax therefore lands mostly on the denominator and drags the ratio down under the bar. ⚠️ **I nearly reported that green as a refutation of the predecessor finding** — a fire before me had a red, I had a green on the same tree, and the tempting story was "not reproducible". It was reproducible; my instrument was cold. ➡️ **Rule for any future p95/perf measurement: discard the first run against a newly-created worktree or a newly-started dev server, or warm it with a throwaway run first.** A cheap tell is wall-clock — if the run takes multiples of its usual time, the numbers in it are not comparable to anything. ⓘ The bisect that produced the predecessor row was run AFTER the cache was warm and re-used one server generation throughout, and its boundary was confirmed by two independent passes, so it is not affected. 💡 **The class: a warm-up artefact does not add noise, it adds BIAS — and bias that flatters your hypothesis is the kind you stop looking for.**

Swept the class: exactly **2 members** repo-wide (`PB-01+02`, `TP-01+02`). **(2) MY `isDecl` HEURISTIC COUNTED A MENTION AS A DECLARATION** — `W1-02` was harvested from a bullet in `e5-deepwater-bundle.md` describing *“the W1-02 water shader, grown up”*. 🚫 **RECOMMENDATION: NOTHING TO BUILD — AND DO NOT BUILD A specs-vs-BACKLOG SLICE-ID GUARD.** Three independent reasons, the third of which is new and is the real contribution: **(a)** it would red **16 rows** against a ledger measured clean; **(b)** its denominator must encode a **seven-way document-class distinction that exists nowhere in the filesystem** — status is a line, never a filename, by house convention; **(c) ⭐ ABSENCE FROM THE LEDGER IS BIDIRECTIONAL.** §4 requires finished rungs to be **retired** from the ladder, so *“absent from BACKLOG”* is equally the signature of **never-started** work and of **completed-and-retired** work — **3 of my 16 (19%) were the latter.** A guard firing on absence cannot tell the two apart, so **it would report finished work as missing** — the false-NOT-DONE shape F-1368-1 named, mechanised and put on a 5-minute cadence. 💡 **THE THROUGH-LINE, AND IT CLOSES THE SET RATHER THAN EXTENDING IT.** s1369: your freshly-built instrument is the most dangerous artifact on a dry board. s1370: the instrument can be right and the inference wrong. s1371: the result can be fabricated because the probe never ran. **s1372: THE INSTRUMENT, THE INFERENCE AND THE PROBE CAN ALL BE SOUND — AND THE *QUESTION* STILL WRONG, BECAUSE IT ASSUMED A KEY THE LEDGER DOES NOT USE.** Both surfaces s1370 offered have now been swept and both dissolved the same way, which is itself the finding: **this factory’s ledger is organised by THREAD, and every audit that joins on a minted ID — F-ids, slice IDs — will keep rediscovering that fact at the cost of a fire.** ➡️ **The rule I’d hand forward: before measuring what an index is missing, verify that the thing you are joining on is the index’s KEY. Ask what the ledger is organised BY, not what tokens appear in it.** ⓘ And the honest footnote: the ST-00..ST-07 block looked like the best finding available to this fire — 8 slices, owner-ratified *yesterday*, in no ledger — and it took one `grep` of the defence to dissolve it. **s1370’s rule (“ask what would make this innocent, and go read THAT”) is what turned a dramatic false finding into a paragraph.**

🟢 **F-1371-1 (s1371, MEASURED — NEGATIVE RESULT: NO FINDING IS LOST IN `reviews/`, BECAUSE F-IDS ARE NOT THE LEDGER’S KEY — AND MY OWN INSTRUMENT WAS WRONG THREE TIMES, THE LAST TIME BY A SHELL EXIT CODE WEARING A MEASUREMENT’S CLOTHES.)** 🧭 **THE PROBE.** s1370 §K(3) offered two surfaces as *hypotheses, not work*: `reviews/*.md` findings that never became F-ids, and `specs/**` slices no leaf claims. 🟢 **F-1370-1 (s1370, MEASURED — NEGATIVE RESULT ACROSS THE FULL DENOMINATOR: NOT ONE OF THE 507 CLOSED GOAL LEAVES RESTS ON A PREMISE THAT LATER CHANGED — AND I REFUTED MY OWN HYPOTHESIS THREE TIMES GETTING THERE.)** 🧭 **THE PROBE, AND WHY IT WAS GENUINELY UNRUN.** s1368 §L(3) and s1369 §K(4) both named it and neither ran it: *“nobody has checked the ~505 CLOSED goal leaves for one that closed on a premise that later changed.”* s1368 audited the **18 OPEN** leaves, s1369 the **78 desk rows**; the closed set is the third and largest enumeration, and it is the one where a rotted premise is **silent by construction** — a closed leaf is read by nobody and reds nothing. 📐 **METHOD, CHOSEN AGAINST s1369’S LESSON: I DELIBERATELY PREFERRED READING A SMALL SET AT SOURCE OVER CLASSIFYING A LARGE ONE.** Walking `goals.json` with the concat-`subgoals`+`tasks` walker: **523 status-carrying nodes** — which **independently re-confirms s1369’s and s1364’s 523/18 to the unit, by a third instrument**. "planned" : task.status`, so a leaf whose hash stopped being ancestral **falls back to `planned`** and the subgoal progress counters drop. **The dashboard, not the guard, is the full-denominator ancestry detector; the 10-sample is belt-and-braces.** 🚫 **RECOMMENDATION: NOTHING TO BUILD, AND SPECIFICALLY DO NOT “WIDEN” THE 10-SAMPLE TO 478.** It would re-implement, on a 5-minute cadence, a check the dashboard already performs every 60 seconds with a louder failure mode. A false NOT-DONE ships nothing, so nothing reds, no gate fires, and the cost is invisible: it is simply an action that never gets asked for. **The tell is a leaf whose remaining-work list has more nouns than its blocker list** — that gap is where a finished noun goes to hide. WHEN ONE FILE HOLDS BOTH A MEASUREMENT AND A CONCLUSION, THE CONCLUSION INHERITS THE MEASUREMENT'S AUTHORITY WITHOUT INHERITING ITS SCOPE.** `hero-credit-log.json` earned trust by being right about hero to the second — and spent it on `stoppedBeforeNextCharacter: true`, a claim about a character its instrument never observed. **That is why the sentence survived s1350 quoting this exact file, s1366 reading it and flagging the anomaly, and sixteen fires in between:** everything verifiable around it checks out. ➡️ **The rule I'd hand forward: when a document reports a number and then draws a conclusion, ask what the instrument's DENOMINATOR was, and whether the conclusion stays inside it. Within one extension sat takes *and* the picks among them, and the picks are irreplaceable for a reason no extension can see: **they are not data, they are a decision about data.** ➡️ **The rule I'd hand forward: when you inherit a classification, do not just re-check which bucket things fell into — ask what question the buckets were built to answer, and whether it is the question you now need answered.** A taxonomy built to find "what can't be regenerated?" cannot find "what wouldn't be the same if it were", and *the second question is the one that matters for anything a human chose.*

🟡 **F-1346-1 (s1346, MEASURED — s1345 §H(3) ASKED FOR A PROBE FOR ROWS WHOSE SUBJECT IS A *DOCUMENT*; IT IS BUILT, AND ITS FIRST RESULT IS THAT MOST OPEN ROWS ARE NOT PROBEABLE AT ALL).** s1345 cleared the five cheapest CODE-subject rows with `git log` plus a read, then named the gap: the remainder argue about a guard's source, a law surface, an inventory or a master, and *"those need a different probe than `git log`, and nobody has designed one."* ✓ **BUILT: `scripts/row-quote-currency.mjs`.** These rows are unusually quotable — they cite a path and then quote the exact sentence they are arguing about — so the probe asks one question per quote: **does that verbatim string still occur in a file the row names?** Proximity to a path citation decides *whether* a quote is checkable; the union of every path the row names decides the *verdict* (both halves were measured necessary — see F-1346-2). 📊 **LIVE RESULT, and the headline is the denominator, not the hit rate: of 61 open rows, 28 offer NOTHING checkable and only 41 quotes across 33 rows can be asked at all.** Of those 41, **15 present / 26 gone**; rows rank ABSENT 20 / PRESENT 13 / UNRESOLVED 28. ⚠️ **ABSENT RANKS A ROW FOR PROBING — IT IS NOT A CLOSURE AND NOT A DEFECT**, and I am naming the three false-positive classes I measured rather than leaving them for the next reader to rediscover: a quoted line later **EXTENDED** (F-1336-2 — `AP-08 — THE ALPHA EXCHANGE + THE COUNTY FAIR` is alive and well in the spec; a `; lineage: …` was appended after the row quoted it), a **shell command** quoted as evidence (F-1336-3), and a quote of **another ROW** rather than a file. ⚖️ **AND ABSENCE HAS NO DIRECTION, WHICH IS THE LIMIT THAT MATTERS:** a row may quote text asserting what IS in a file (gone ⇒ premise rotted) or the text it says is MISSING and ought to be added (gone ⇒ the row is still LIVE). F-1284-1 is the second kind — `"Bash(bash scripts/deploy.sh)"` is genuinely absent from the settings file, and that absence is the finding, not its expiry. **A verdict still requires reading the row.** ⓘ Also worth the next fire's minute: a row is flagged if **any one** of its quotes is gone, so output is sorted by the FRACTION gone — **F-1305-1 and F-1345-1 both flag ABSENT while the sentence each is actually arguing about is still in place** (I grepped both). **GATE: none — the instrument is committed and self-tested. Its output is a triage ORDER for a future fire, and must not be used to strike a row without reading it.**

🟡 **F-1346-2 (s1346, PROVEN ON MYSELF — MY OWN INSTRUMENT'S SELF-TEST PASSED ON A BUILD THAT WAS ABOUT TO PUBLISH A SPECTACULAR FALSE HEADLINE, BECAUSE CONTROLS MEASURE THE SPECIFICATION AND NOT THE INTENT).** The first build of `scripts/row-quote-currency.mjs` reported **ABSENT 41 / PRESENT 1** on the live ledger — i.e. *"almost every open row's premise has vanished"*, which would have been the best paragraph in this handoff and was **entirely false**. ✓ **ROOT CAUSE:** a code-span regex matched the prose sitting **BETWEEN two adjacent backtick spans**, so ordinary ledger narration was harvested as "quotes" attributed to files that never contained it. Tokenising by alternation (odd segments of a split on the delimiter) is the only correct read; the regex is now impossible to reintroduce silently because a **regression control for exactly that string shape** sits in the self-test. 🔁 **THEN IT HAPPENED A SECOND TIME, DIFFERENTLY:** the fix scored each quote against its **nearest** path citation, which looked more precise and was measurably worse — F-1294-1 quotes a sentence that genuinely lives in `scripts/fire.md`, but its nearest citation was `playwright.config.ts`, so an **intact premise was called GONE**. Cure: proximity decides whether a quote is checkable, the union of all named paths decides the verdict. 🪞 **THE PART WORTH INHERITING: the self-test PASSED on the first build, and on the second.** Six controls, all green, all correct — they proved the code did what I had specified, and the specification was the thing that was wrong. **Every one of the three defects was caught the same way instead: by taking a handful of the live verdicts and checking them by hand against the real files** (`grep -c` on the spec, the inventory, the guard header). ➡️ **The rule: a green self-test licenses you to trust the mechanism, never the measurement. ✅ **F-1298-2 (s1298) STRUCK s1345 — CURED IN CODE 2026-07-31 by `818aa398`, AND ITS ROW HAD READ "GATE: none. Same code, same gate, opposite rulings, 4.2× apart. **An unqualified "measure it" gate gets answered by the cheapest harness, and the cheapest harness is idle — the one condition guaranteed NOT to exercise the input the finding is about.** 🔒 **BOTH growth vectors were then bounded, so 12.66 KiB is close to a real ceiling, not a sample:** **(i) `orders` is hard-capped** — `src/agent/StandingOrders.ts` `validateStandingOrders` rejects with *"orders may contain at most 32 entries."* (measured: a 200-order payload is refused), and `validateOrder` byte-bounds every entry genuinely unbounded one and it is slow:** `src/agent/View.ts` pushes one `waveEntry` per wave with **no truncation** and emits the whole array every view, measured at **~114–121 B/wave** (clean linear: w2:1, w3:2, w4:3 entries) — but real contracts **terminate at wave 2–4**, so reaching 64 KiB from the driven ceiling needs **~450 more waves than any contract produces**. ⚖️ **HONEST VERDICT: the `ValueError` is unreachable today** — but at 19.8% of the limit the margin is one schema change wide (a raised order cap, or a per-wave field, eats it), which is exactly why the gate's order-of-magnitude test is the right one and why it now says cure. ⛔ **WHY A FIRE CANNOT FINISH IT, AND THIS SHARPENS s1351's CANDIDATE NOTE RATHER THAN CONTRADICTING IT:** F-1351-1 banked this row as 🟡 **F-1344-2 (s1344, MEASURED — THE LEDGER'S OPEN/CLOSED VOCABULARY IS ENTIRELY LEDGER-INTERNAL, SO A FINDING CURED IN *CODE* STAYS "OPEN" FOREVER AND READS AS QUEUEABLE).** `findings-state-guard` exists because *"a reader following the open rows would spend a lane re-fixing shipped work"* (its own header) — but it detects only a 🟡 row **contradicted by a ✅ row**. When work is cured in code and **no closure row is ever written**, there is no contradiction to find: `double-state` reads **0** and the guard is green while the row still advertises the work. ✓ **SPECIMEN, first row I probed:** F-1320-1 (terrain seed re-parsed per noise hash) was cured by `992f4066` at **2026-08-01T08:49** — `terrainSeedCache` now memoises on `window.location.search` — while its row still led 🟡. ⚖️ **HONEST CALIBRATION, because the two cases are NOT the same disease:** F-1320-1's lag was **~11 hours** — ordinary, blameless drain bookkeeping, *not* rot; F-1344-1's was **21 days**. The finding is not that fires are sloppy, it is that **no instrument would ever notice either one**, so the 11-hour case and the 21-day case are indistinguishable from inside the ledger. ⓘ **CONSEQUENCE FOR ANY FIRE READING "61 open":** that census counts *declarations*, not live defects — it is an upper bound on queueable work, never a worklist. Probe the code before authoring against any 🟡 row. **GATE: none — this is a caution with a specimen, not a mechanism; a real cure would have to compare ledger claims to code, which is not mechanically decidable in general. I did NOT build one rather than ship a guard that greens on the easy half and hides the rest.**

✅ **F-1343-1 (s1343, MEASURED + CLOSED-BY-MECHANISM — A FIRE THAT IS PERMISSION-DENIED HAS NOWHERE TO PUT THE WORK, SO IT PUTS IT IN PROSE, AND PROSE IS NOT A QUEUE).** s1342 composed the custody rule for `.claude/skills/drain/SKILL.md`, was denied by the harness, and filed it as a sentence inside its handoff. ✓ **I re-hit the identical denial this fire** (attempted the edit myself rather than inherit the claim; the harness refused, and I did **not** route around it via Bash). That is **three fires — s1295, s1342, s1343 — composing the same text and none able to land it**, which makes this a class, not an incident. 🔍 **MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED: no surface for this exists.** `find` over the repo for `*attended*` → **zero hits**; no `tasks/attended/`, `tasks/owner/`, `tasks/blocked/`, `docs/attended*`, `ATTENDED*.md`, `PENDING*.md`. The `tasks/` tree is exactly `running · janitor · failed · done · queue/{art,lane-a..d,main} · runs`. The nearest mechanism, `tasks/janitor/*.req` (`lane-runner-v3.sh:118-149`), is a **whitelisted two-op relay** (`refresh-lane`, clean-artifacts) — not a general park-an-edit facility. 🔑 **AND THE OWNER'S DESK STRUCTURALLY CANNOT HOLD THESE, WHICH IS THE REAL FINDING.** The desk's 🔺 is an owner-**routing** axis and BACKLOG's 🟡/✅ is a census-**visibility** axis; `desk-declaration-guard.mjs:26-34` explicitly forbids conflating them (citing refuted F-1334-1). **Neither axis can express the distinction that matters here:** a **RULING** only Robin can make (design fork, canon, money) versus an **ACTION** any unrestricted shell can perform in thirty seconds. So s1342's paste request sits in the same undifferentiated prose list as genuine design forks, **queuing behind decisions it does not need**. 🔒 **MECHANISM: `tasks/attended-owed/` + `scripts/attended-owed-audit.mjs`**, wired into `test:ledger-guards` (which every fire runs as its last act, F-1300-4) and grandfathered in `gate-caller-baseline.json` with its reason — it inherits `test:ledger-guards`'s deliberate orphanhood exactly as `status-archive-audit.mjs` does. ⚖️ **THE TEETH ARE DELIBERATELY ASYMMETRIC, and that asymmetry is the design, not timidity:** LANDED-but-not-archived and malformed/bad-target are **rc 1** (a *fire* can fix those); a merely **OPEN** item is **rc 0** (only the attended side can clear it, and a permanently-red guard is flagged past within a fire or two — the exact fate that makes a gate worthless). OPEN items are *printed* every fire instead. `--strict` reds them for an attended sweep. 🎯 **"LANDED" IS NEVER A CLAIM ANYBODY MAKES — it is `target` containing `anchor`, verified by reading the destination file.** That is s1342's own through-line mechanised: *before writing `GATE: none` because you did the thing, ask what a reader would have to READ to know you did it* — here the reader is a script, and what it reads is the target. ✅ **Teeth PROVEN by manufacturing every branch, not by a green** (the s1299/s1301 standard — a passing guard never executes its violation path): MALFORMED **rc=1**, BAD-TARGET **rc=1**, LANDED-NOT-ARCHIVED **rc=1** (read the anchor out of a real target file), OPEN **rc=0**, `--strict` OPEN **rc=1**. Both probes **archived, not deleted** (Retention Law; `rm` is blocked here by design and CLAUDE.md §4.10 wants the `mv` anyway). ⓘ **A trap closed before it was sprung:** the glob would have swallowed the directory's own `README.md` as a malformed item and red the guard — caught by asking what the glob would eat *before* writing the README, and skipped explicitly. ⛔ **The first item, `001-drain-skill-custody-rule.md`, is OPEN and carries the exact paste text** — attended, ~60 seconds. 💡 *Reusable shape: **a permission boundary silently converts work into narration.** The fire did everything right — composed the text, refused to bypass the gate, wrote it down — and the output was still a paragraph nobody is scheduled to read. When a process cannot perform an act, give it somewhere to put the act; otherwise the only container left is the handoff, and a handoff is read once by one successor who has its own priorities.*

🟡 **F-1349-1 (s1349, MEASURED — THE REASON THAT PARKED `tasks/attended-owed/001-drain-skill-custody-rule.md` FOR SIX FIRES WAS TRUE, BUT ITS IMPLIED CURE WAS MEASURED WORTHLESS).** The item has been printed at every fire since s1343 under the reason *"Fires cannot write .claude/ (F-1027-4)"* — carried, never re-run. s1349 ran it (Mistake #4: VERIFY-DON'T-INHERIT). ✓ **The denial reproduces**: `Edit` on `.claude/skills/drain/SKILL.md` → *"requested permissions to write … but you haven't granted it yet"*. ✓ **CONTROL, same tool, same session, non-`.claude` path** (`logs/session-scratch/s1349-lock.txt`) → **succeeded**. 🔺 **F-1349-2 (s1349, HAZARD — OPENED WITH ITS CURE, NO OWNER ACTION NEEDED: THE `attended-owed` MECHANISM HAD NO RULE AGAINST LANDING AN ITEM BY ROUTING AROUND THE DENIAL THAT CREATED IT).** Neither `tasks/attended-owed/README.md` nor `scripts/attended-owed-audit.mjs` said anything about *how not to* clear an item. ⚠️ **And the gap is live, not theoretical: `Bash(node:*)`, `Bash(cat:*)`, `Bash(cp:*)` and `Bash(mv:*)` are all on the fire allowlist** (`.claude/settings.json`), so a fire almost certainly **could** write a `.claude/` target from a shell. **I did not attempt it, and that refusal is the finding's point** — the boundary on `.claude/` exists to stop an autonomous agent editing its own instruction surface, and an agent that complies with one tool and defeats it with another has defeated the control, not honoured it. **The denial is the answer, not an obstacle in front of the answer.** 🎯 **The predictable failure mode is ATTRITION, not ignorance.** These items are by construction cheap, already-decided, fully composed, and re-read at every single fire; item 001 has now been printed **seven** times without landing. The fire most likely to shell around it is a **late** one carrying six predecessors' frustration — so the warning is aimed at that exact moment and says so in those words. ✅ **CURED IN THE SAME COMMIT, at the two surfaces that are actually read:** the class-level rule now heads `tasks/attended-owed/README.md` (read when an item is *opened*), and the per-item `why:` line — **the string the audit prints at every fire** — now ends *"Do NOT shell around it."* 🚫 **Deliberately NOT propagated to `scripts/fire.md`:** the audit's printed line already reaches every fire on the read path, and this corpus's larger standing problem is over-propagation, not under-. 💡 **REUSABLE SHAPE:** a queue built to hold work a process is *forbidden* to do is a standing invitation to do it another way — **whenever you build one, write the anti-bypass rule at the same time**, because the person who needs it is not the person who built it.

🟡 **F-1350-1 (s1350, MEASURED + ACTED — THE DESK ROW CONTAINED ITS OWN UNBLOCKING INSTRUCTION, AND THE "OWNER'S DESK" LABEL OVERRODE IT FOR NINETEEN FIRES).** F-1331-4 has carried the Retention Law's largest hole since s1331 as one headline: **AT RISK 748 files / 566.47 MB**. (2) `781079ed` — **133 files / 0.152 MB**, the motion-pilot RECIPE slice. 🔑 **AND THE SECOND SALVAGE IS THE REAL FIND, because a byte count ranks retention exactly backwards.** Inside the 557 MB nobody had ever described, **133 of the 771 at-risk files (17.3% of the files, 0.027% of the bytes) are `.json` per-take API logs, `.md` run notes and the `generate-videos.mjs` generator** — the record of *how the pose library was made*, including `pose-library/hero/RUN-NOTE.md`'s dated *"QA BLOCKED; task stopped at the 800-credit floor"*. **The other 569 MB is `.png`/`.mp4` output regenerable from exactly those files.** ⚠️ **CORRECTED s1366 (F-1366-1): that last sentence is true of 94.81% of those bytes and FALSE of the curated 5.19%** — 20 of the png files are the *picks* (3 Deliverable sheets + the 12 best-of-three selections + 5 four-view composites), and a **stochastic, paid** generator cannot re-produce a chosen frame. **The RECIPE/OUTPUT split was the right first cut and the wrong last word: it sorts by extension, and "someone chose this one" is invisible to an extension.** Those 20 files / 28.92 MB are now salvaged (`ca534290`). A hole sorted by bytes puts the irreplaceable part last and it rode along, blocked, for weeks — **the Retention Law's own words are "run logs, fire logs, reports, evidence", i.e. precisely the 0.027% the framing buried.** 📉 **NET: AT RISK 748 files / 566.47 MB → 602 files / 556.81 MB; LOCAL-ONLY 0; SALVAGED 6 → 152.** ⚖️ **F-1331-4 IS NOT CLOSED AND WAS DELIBERATELY NOT PRE-EMPTED — the 638 png/mp4 files / 569.24 MB it asks a ruling on are untouched**, because that ruling is a question about repo *weight* and neither salvaged slice has any. What changed is that **nothing unrecoverable now depends on the answer**, so the ruling is no longer urgent, only pending. 🧾 **Composition, so the one word is cheap** (`s1350-motionpilot.mjs`): `pose-library` 421.31 MB / 614 files · `production-newsie-mei` 146.69 MB / 123 · `production-bandit-wrecker` 9.28 MB / 41 · `production-bandit-base` 0.02 MB / 2; by type **494.23 MB png, 82.90 MB mp4**; 4 blobs are held twice (18.67 MB git would dedupe anyway); true new weight of a full salvage **~550 MB pre-compression**. ⓘ **Method:** both commits built with `commit-tree` against a **temp index** — main's working tree and index were never touched (§3.0b custody), verified by `git status` after each. ↩️ **VETO WINDOW (§7.4): the second salvage is a fire's judgement call inside a directory the owner has a pending ruling on.** It adds 0.152 MB to a `save/` branch that is never merged to main, so it cannot affect the thing being ruled on. **Reverse with one word — the branch is one ref delete.** 💡 **REUSABLE SHAPE: an item's BADGE is inherited by everything inside it.** A row that is 98% owner-blocked and 2% do-it-now reads, to every triaging reader, as 100% blocked — and the 2% is invisible precisely *because* the 98% is correctly labelled. **When you write a desk row, split the unblocked duty into its own line rather than a clause inside the blocked one**, and when you *read* one, ask what the row would have you do if the owner never answers.

🟡 **F-1343-2 (s1343, MEASURED + INSTRUMENT IMPROVED — "59 COMMITS BEHIND" IS A NUMBER THAT CANNOT BE ACTED ON, BECAUSE IT COUNTS BOOKKEEPING AND CODE IN THE SAME UNIT).** `lane-usable.mjs` prints a behind-count on every USABLE verdict, and its own comment (`:94-97`) argues — **correctly, and I did not override it** — that staleness-enough-to-matter is a property of the TASK, so it refuses to make a fourth verdict word. Of those 59 commits, **ZERO touched `src/`** and zero touched `functions/`; the real drift is **four `e2e/` specs + `package.json`** (14 files once `scripts/` is included, of which 3 are s1341 `tmp-*` probes and one is `fire.md`, a law file). **The other ~54 commits are STATUS.md, artifact screenshots and ledger rows — none of which can affect whether a master RUNS.** ⓘ **The lanes are not neglected:** the s1332 janitor `refresh-lane` requests **did** work (`tasks/janitor/` is empty, requests consumed at 14:35), and main has advanced **exactly 59** commits since — the staleness is one afternoon of fire traffic, not rot. ⚠️ **THE FIND THAT JUSTIFIES THE PATCH: `lane/m3`'s `test:ledger-guards` is a STRICT SUBSET of main's** — it lacks `test:desk-declaration` and `status-archive-audit.mjs` entirely. **A task gated on that lane produces a green that means less than a green on main**, and no existing probe says so. 🔒 **PATCHED:** the USABLE footnote now prints run-surface drift (`src e2e functions scripts` + the configs, deliberately excluding `docs/ tasks/ artifacts/ reviews/ logs/`), names the files, and raises an explicit warning when `package.json` is among them. When drift is empty it says so — *"the gap is bookkeeping only"* — which is a far stronger statement than any count. 🪞 **Honest note on my own method: my first cut of this measurement grepped `^src/`, got **0**, and I nearly wrote "zero code."** The `e2e/` and `package.json` drift was invisible to that filter and I caught it only because a `git diff --stat` contradicted me. **A narrow denominator produced a clean-sounding number that was wrong in the direction of reassurance** — the same shape as s1341's 31→3.

✅ **F-1342-1 (s1342, MEASURED + CLOSED-BY-REPAIR — A CURE THAT WROTE "I HAVE ADOPTED IT" WAS ADOPTED BY EXACTLY ONE FIRE, BECAME NOBODY'S LAW, AND WAS CARRIED AS DONE FOR 47 FIRES).** Sent by s1341 §I(2) to re-measure the FACT-shaped desk remainder, I checked **F-1295-1**, whose closing sentence reads verbatim: *"**GATE: none** — the fire-side cure is free and **I have adopted it this fire**."* The cure is *"never check foreign content into MAIN's working tree to gate it — gate in a detached worktree."* ✓ **MEASURED ACROSS THE WHOLE LAW CORPUS, READ NOT GREPPED — IT IS WRITTEN NOWHERE.** `scripts/fire.md`: **5** `worktree` mentions, every one lane-safety / art-slot / lane-diff-classification, **none about custody**. `.claude/skills/drain/SKILL.md` — **the surface a drainer actually reads — contains the string `worktree` ZERO times.** `CLAUDE.md`: the corpus's only "detached worktrees" is **`:50`, Mistake #12, for *attribution runs*** — i.e. **contention**, the question F-1295-1 *itself* explicitly distinguishes (*"this extends the same hygiene to custody, which is the stronger reason"*). `STATUS.md`: all **140** `^- **s9` bullets swept — and the denominator is worth stating exactly, because the habitual shorthand "140 law bullets" over-states the law corpus **7.8×**: it is **18 genuine lettered law bullets** (`s9i`, `s9ab`, `s9al`, `s9ar`, `s9at`, `s9au`, …) **plus 119 numeric handoff archives**. `worktree` hits across all of them are the 4-lane protocol (`s9i`), the `s9al` worktree salvage, and the `s9ab` lane lifecycle — **no custody rule anywhere**. `AGENTS.md`: **no hits**. 🔑 **THE MECHANISM IS GRAMMATICAL, AND IT IS THE EXACT MIRROR OF s1341's THROUGH-LINE.** s1341 found that *an imperative has no tense* — a discharged gate still reads as an order. **This is the inverse: a PERFECT TENSE has no subject that outlives it.** *"I have adopted it"* describes a completed, durable-sounding state, so every later reader scanning a 🟡 row for owed work correctly sees **nothing owed** — but the *"I"* was a single process that exited minutes later, and adoption by a process is not adoption by a factory. **`GATE: none` was true of the owner and false of the board**, and no instrument distinguishes those two readings. ⚠️ **The harm is not hypothetical, because the defect it cures is the one with no detector:** a HOLD verdict has **no enforcement surface in git**, `git status` cannot see a sweep (a sweep's signature is the *absence* of dirt), and `git checkout HEAD -- <paths>` **restores from a HEAD that has itself moved** — so the fire that gets swept goes on believing its verdict held. 🔒 **REPAIRED: `scripts/fire.md` §3.0b** now carries the rule as standing law, with the `b37c1fc6` incident, the reason every available probe is blind, and the HOLD-has-no-enforcement-surface consequence. ⛔ **ONE HALF I COULD NOT CLOSE, AND IT IS THE HIGHER-TRAFFIC SURFACE:** `.claude/skills/drain/SKILL.md` is **not writable from the fire shell** (the The drain skill therefore still has no custody precondition — **ATTENDED, one paste, the text is §3.0b's** and it belongs beside the existing clean-main bullet in its §0. ⓘ **SCOPE STATED HONESTLY: F-1295-1 measured the WORKING-TREE case only.** Gating via `git merge --no-ff` and planning to revert on a red puts undecided content on **HEAD** instead — structurally the same bet against concurrency, **UNMEASURED**; §3.0b records it as a caution and explicitly forbids citing it as proven. I did **not** stretch the finding to cover it. 💡 *Reusable shape: **a ledger row can close itself by describing its own author's behaviour.** "I have adopted it" is the most dangerous sentence a fire can write, because it is simultaneously TRUE, verifiable, and worthless to everyone who comes after — the factory has no memory of a process, only of files. **Before writing `GATE: none` because you did the thing, ask what a reader would have to READ to know you did it.** If the answer is "your handoff", the gate is not none.*

✅ **F-1342-2 (s1342, MEASURED — AN OWNER-DESK BUG REPORT DESCRIBES A DEFECT THAT ITS OWN CITED SCREENSHOT REFUTES; IT HAD BEEN CARRIED SINCE s1257).** Running s1341 §I(2)'s currency sweep I re-measured **F-1257-4** (*"at 390px the HUD **WEAPON** panel clips its subtitle mid-word: `the Prospector  Lo` with `suggest-only` wrapping below"*) and **the symptom does not exist.** ✓ **There is no subtitle being clipped because there is no single subtitle STRING** — `src/ui/Hud.ts` writes **three separate elements**: `:256` name `'the Prospector'`, `:257` level `` `L${snapshot.agent?.permissionLevel ?? 0}` ``, `:258` label `'suggest-only'`. ⭐ **The `Lo` read as a mid-word truncation is `L0` — L followed by the DIGIT ZERO**, the default permission level, gold-coloured by `styles.css:1019–1021` and set in the panel's serif face at 0.72rem/weight-800, where a zero closely resembles an `o`. **And `suggest-only` on the next line is `grid-column: 1 / -1` (`styles.css:1023–1024`) — its own full-width row, BY CONSTRUCTION.** 🔍 **The screenshot also disproves the claim on its own terms:** `[data-hud-agent-name]` carries `text-overflow: ellipsis` (`:1013–1017`), so a truncated name would render **`the Prospect…`** — the cited PNG shows **`the Prospector` complete, no ellipsis**. ✓ **No repair could have masked this**: `src/styles.css` last moved `52fa15ad` (2026-07-26) and `src/ui/Hud.ts` `e5bd6260` (2026-07-22) — **both untouched since before F-1257-4 was written.** 🔑 **THE CLASS, AND IT IS THE COMPLEMENT OF THIS REPO'S USUAL FAILURE.** The house law is *evidence, not vibes* — and F-1257-4 **had** evidence: a real screenshot, from a real plain boot, at the right viewport. **It was read like prose instead of like a DOM.** Three adjacent inline elements in one visual line are indistinguishable from one wrapped string **to the eye**, and a glyph rendered small in a serif face is ambiguous **to the eye** — so a screenshot is a rich source about *appearance* and a **near-worthless one about STRUCTURE**, which is exactly what a "clipping" claim is about. ⚠️ **The cost is asymmetric and it is why this is a finding rather than a shrug: a false NEGATIVE from a screenshot wastes nobody's time, but a false POSITIVE mints an owner action** — and this one sat on the desk for **85 fires**, re-listed every handoff, asking Robin to rule on the rendering of the number zero. 💡 *Reusable shape: **before reporting a visual defect, read the code that produced the pixels.** If your claim is about structure — clipped, wrapped, overlapping, mis-aligned — the screenshot is the SYMPTOM and the DOM is the EVIDENCE; a bug report that never left the image is a description of your own eyesight. **Cheap discriminator: ask what the defect would have looked like if it were real.** Here it would have carried an ellipsis, and it did not.*

✅ **F-1341-1 (s1341, CLOSED-BY-REPAIR — THREE HANDOFF LINE-1s WERE OFF THE LIVE BOARD, AND THE NEWEST ONE WAS THE PRIORITY LIST THE NEXT FIRE WAS SUPPOSED TO WORK FROM).** `scripts/fire.md` §4 orders a fire taking the lock to move the previous line-1 down into a `- **s<N> ... (line-1 archive):**` bullet. That step is done by hand every fire, so it can be skipped in silence — and no guard read for it. ✓ **Found at source, not inferred:** s1340's lock commit `f2380ccc` shows `STATUS.md | 2 +-` — **one line replaced, no compensating bullet** — destroying s1339's 8,223-char handoff; s1340 then died (48 min stale by owning-commit time, §1.3's timezone-proof test) so its own handoff never put the line back. 🔍 **Confirmed absent from the working tree entirely**, not merely moved: `grep -rl` over every tracked `*.md` found s1337's dropped handoff **nowhere** — no rotation file, no sibling ledger. 🔬 **F-1274-3 (s1274, MEASURED AT THE RAW + CURED — CONFIRMS F-1269-2, AND NARROWS s1273'S READING OF IT) — THE LANE ARM'S "77.61% IDLE" WAS A READING OF AN IDLE MACHINE TAKEN AFTER THE WORK FINISHED, AND IT WAS PRINTED AS "idle during 8-child arm".** `logs/session-scratch/s1268/child-scaling-v2.mjs:53-59` schedules its one CPU observation with a hard-coded `setTimeout(…, 3500)`. Two measured facts make that a claim rather than a measurement: **(1)** `top -l 2` is not instantaneous — three consecutive runs on this machine took **1815 / 1786 / 1780 ms**, and the block v2 parses is the **SECOND** sample, so the kept reading corresponds to ~3500+~1000 ms in and the command does not return until **~5290 ms** in; **(2)** the two arms differ ~2.4× in length — the fire arm's 8-child reps ran **10.14 / 10.50 / 9.92 s** (3500 ms = ~36% in, a genuine mid-arm reading that captured all eight children at ~54.5% CPU each), while the **lane** arm's ran **4.06 / 4.18 / 4.33 s**. 🔑 **PROVEN AT THE RAW CAPTURE, NOT INFERRED FROM THE EMPTY ARRAY** — the alternative explanation (an nvm-node naming difference defeating the `\bnode\b` filter) is refuted by `topRaw` in `child-scaling-lane.json`: it reads **"3 running"** and contains **no node process anywhere in a list sorted BY CPU** (top entry `com.apple.Virtua` at **20.7%**). Eight saturated children cannot be absent from a CPU-sorted list. **The children had already exited: a timing failure, not a filter failure.** ⚠️ **SCOPE — THIS NARROWS s1273's §E2, WHICH SAID LEAVING IT BROKEN "POISONS AN OWNER-GATED DECISION".** It does not. F-1270-4 states its confirming test in **throughput multipliers** (*"~7–12× confirms the mechanism, ~3× refutes it"*), and those come from `runN()`'s hrtime around child exit — **a separate and sound path**. Only the *corroborating* idle/child-CPU field was invalid, and only on the short arm. **v2's CONCLUSION stands; one of its supporting fields did not.** The fix still matters because the owner will RUN this instrument, and it would print a false label at the moment of confirmation. 🔒 **CURE: `logs/session-scratch/s1274/child-scaling-v3.mjs`** (new file — **v2 and both its result JSONs left byte-untouched per the Retention Law**). The throughput half is deliberately **unchanged**, including the workload constant, so the numbers stay comparable with the v2 runs. What changed: the delay is **derived from the median 8-child time this machine just measured** (`fraction 0.5`, compensated for top's own second-sample latency) instead of a constant; the run records `topInvokedAtMs` / `topReturnedAtMs` / `topLatencyMs` / `childrenAliveAtTopInvoke` / `childrenAliveAtTopReturn` so the label is **falsifiable by the reader**; and **the label is earned or withheld** — a reading with zero child rows is marked `INVALID … Do NOT read idlePercent as arm load` and never called "during". An arm too short to contain a valid sample is **skipped and said so** — *an unsampled arm reports nothing, not idle*. 🧪 **BOTH DIRECTIONS EXERCISED:** **fire arm, real run** → `IN-ARM: 8 child row(s) observed, 8/8 still alive when top returned`, idle 44.12%, children ~63.4% each (v2's blind luck on the long arm is now v3's guarantee) · **short-arm mutant** (a copy with the workload cut 9e8→3e7, v3 itself untouched) → 8-child arm **0.18 s** → `observation: SKIPPED — arm ~0.18s is too short … NO SAMPLE TAKEN`, where v2 would have slept 3500 ms and printed an idle number. ⓘ **Stated honestly: the third branch (children die *while* top runs → `INVALID`) is a defensive backstop and was NOT exercised** — with the 0.5 fraction and the 300 ms floor the schedule avoids that regime by construction, so it only fires if load shifts between the reps and the observation.

🔻 **F-1256-3 (s1256, MEASURED — SMALL, CHEAP, AND IT BIT ME TWICE IN ONE FIRE).** `scripts/citation-title-guard.mjs` scans **tracked** `.md` only, so **a newly authored master's citations are invisible to it until the authoring commit lands** — which is exactly one step too late, because the house pattern is *run the guards, then commit*. Measured here by accident: the guard reported **PASS, 310 scanned** with my new master sitting untracked in the tree, then **FAIL** on that same file's `e2e/helpers/hero-approach.ts:5` (`export async function moveHeroTo(page: Page, x: number, z: number): Promise<void> {`; inlined in `e2e/release-build.spec.ts` until `af48a749` retired the duplicate — pointer repaired s1259, the claim below is unchanged) the moment `47f5f0aa` made it tracked (`found 2`). Both citations were bare the whole time; only the guard's visibility changed. **Consequence: every fire that authors a master and gates before committing gets a free false green**, and the failure only surfaces on some later fire's unrelated run — where it looks like that fire's fault. Not urgent (the guard does catch it eventually, and it caught mine), but the fix is small: scan the working tree, or have the authoring path re-run the guard after `git add`. Until then, **authoring fires should run `test:citations` a second time after the commit** — this fire did, which is the only reason its own master is clean.

✅ **F-1247-1 (s1247, MEASURED + FIXED THIS FIRE, `e66af39d`) — THE GATE BATTERY'S OWN SELECTOR COULD REPORT A GREEN OVER A BATTERY IT SILENTLY NARROWED, AND IT IS THE EXACT SHAPE THE FILE REFUSES TWICE IN ITS OWN COMMENTS.** `scripts/run-guards.mjs:158` built its changed-file set as `` `${diff.stdout}\n${untracked.status === 0 ? untracked.stdout : ''}` `` — so **any** failure of `git ls-files --others --exclude-standard` contributed an **empty string** instead of stopping. ⚠️ **This is the same failure-as-absence class as F-1246-1, and s1246's scope sweep could not have found it:** that sweep hunted the `try/catch → ''` shape, and **`spawnSync` never throws** — the conversion here is a **ternary on `status === 0`**, invisible to a catch-pattern grep. 🔬 **PROVED BY EXECUTION, NOT BY READING, with the single variable isolated.** A PATH shim failed *only* `ls-files --others` and passed every other git call through. Subject: the harness's own **"Shape 1"** — a brand-new **unstaged** `functions/api/_accounts.ts`, invisible to `git diff`, so the untracked union is the *only* thing that can pull in the worker guards. **Treatment: `rc=0`, `0 file(s) changed since HEAD`, `(no path rule matched -- base gate only)`, `guards: 3/3 passed`.** **Control, identical fixture, real git: `guards: 6/6 passed`, `+ test:stats, test:accounts, test:mp <- 1 file(s) in functions/**`.** ➡️ **A transient listing failure silently deleted three guards from the battery and printed a green.** 🎯 **REACHABILITY, MEASURED AND REPORTED HONESTLY — the ENOBUFS route is NOT the live one.** `git ls-files --others --exclude-standard` on this repo is **53 bytes / 1 file = 0.0% of the 1 MB default cap** (`worktrees/art`'s 566 MB is `.gitignore`d, so `--exclude-standard` never lists it), and that set is bounded by working-tree dirt, which the path-scoped-commit law keeps near zero. The reachable path is a **transient fork failure under load**: `diff` and `ls-files` are **separate spawns**, so one can fail while the other succeeds, and this factory routinely generates the load. `maxBuffer` was raised to 64 MB anyway, but **the check is the fix; the buffer is a belt.** ⚖️ **WHY IT IS A REAL DEFECT AND NOT A NIT: the file convicts itself.** Lines 142–143 — *"A bad ref must be LOUD. Falling back to the gate set would silently run a narrower battery than the caller asked for -- **the exact shape this file refuses**"* — and 165–166 — *"silently narrowing to nothing would report a green over zero guards, which is the failure mode this runner exists to refuse."* Both are enforced with `process.exit(2)`. **The third fork had the principle stated and the mechanism missing** — a ratified-law-without-its-mechanism, one file wide. `status` is compared against `0` rather than tested for truthiness because a signal-killed or never-spawned child yields **`null`**. 🧪 **THE ARM IS FOLDED IN, AND IT IS NOT TAUTOLOGICAL.** Added to `scripts/run-guards.test.mjs` as the **sibling of the existing bad-ref arm** — which was the tell: the suite asserted the loud-on-failure law for the `diff` fork and **never** for the `untracked` fork, the same omission as the code.
